items.statement: Structural and energetic effect of the two Hap orientations
items.expected: Establish the structural and energetic difference between the S4 and C2h orientations of neutral-singlet gas-phase Ir2(Hap)4, retaining all 54 atoms and matched Ir identities. Determine both Ir-Ir distances and G(C2h)-G(S4) at 298.15 K under one standard-state and thermal/low-frequency convention. The reference S4 structure has a shorter Ir-Ir contact and lower Gibbs energy than C2h. Interpret the two structures and relative stability from actual relaxed geometries, energy components and stationary-character evidence; electronic DeltaE is not DeltaG. The source distances 2.599/2.724 A and 9.7 kcal/mol are context, not numerical gates. A physically established model-sensitive difference can pass when the same orientations and states are tracked, any changed stationary character is demonstrated, and the revised structural/energetic inference is bounded accordingly. This result does not itself identify the orbital cause or prove an equilibrium conformer population.

items.statement: Metal–iminoxolene mixing and occupations enable net Ir–Ir π bonding
items.expected: Actual electronic evidence supports metal–iminoxolene mixing that leaves available metal dπ acceptor character and enables a net positive Ir–Ir π contribution. In a symmetry-adapted description the low occupied 1e manifold is π bonding, while empty 4e carries substantial metal/ligand π-antibonding character; occupied 2e/3e also have weak antibonding contributions. These assignments support a net mechanism rather than treating all occupied metal orbitals as bonding. Equivalent density/orbital representations pass without mandatory labels or partition values. A formal oxidation state or short distance alone fails.

items.statement: Relative coordination-unit orientation changes intermetal donor–acceptor overlap
items.expected: The S4 orientation permits filled metal dπ on one center to overlap with empty metal–iminoxolene π* character on the other. The C2h deformation suppresses this interaction, consistent with its longer Ir–Ir distance and higher energy. Establish this orientation-dependent physical account with spatial/electronic evidence plus the comparable structural-energy result, not just the two distances or numerical ordering. The optimized structures also differ in ligand distortion, so their full energy gap is not a uniquely isolated π-overlap energy. Established physically equivalent explanations pass.

items.statement: Stationary character and model truncation bound the equilibrium and experimental interpretation
items.expected: The S4 Hap structure is a local minimum and the C2h comparison is a first-order saddle, so their Gibbs difference is not an equilibrium ratio of two metastable conformers. Use actual curvature/state evidence to establish that applicability conclusion; completion of a frequency calculation alone is not the result. The Hap model supports a qualitative ligand-assisted molecular Ir–Ir bonding account, but does not quantitatively certify the full Egan crystal distance, SOC response, or a unique physical bond order. A Mayer index, orbital population or MOS-based estimate is definition-dependent; it cannot be asserted as exact experimental bond order 2.34. No new full-Egan or SOC calculation is demanded. If a justified model establishes different stationary character for the same candidate orientations, assess its actual curvature and the resulting conformer inference explicitly rather than imposing the source saddle label; the Hap-to-Egan and definition-dependent bond-order limits still apply.
